title: Indian Railway Finance Corporation Ltd - 543257 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IRFC reports H1 FY27 revenue up over 20% and PAT up over 10%; management reiterates ~INR5 lakh crore AUM target for FY27.
summary.overview: Management said H1 FY27 beat both company guidance and street expectations, with revenue up more than 20% and PAT up more than 10% year on year. The CEO said PAT grew in double digits in five of the last six quarters, the exception being Q4 FY26, which carried provisions for new business under RBI norms. Diversification beyond the Indian Railways single-client model is the core theme, with non-railway lending at margins 2-3.5 times the railway book. The call also covered a large pipeline of railway-linked financing (DFC, high-speed rail, freight JVs) that management expects to start in FY28. Most Q&A was on strategy and shareholder value; the transcript gives no reported Q2 figures beyond the H1 growth rates.

segments.name: Railways (IR) lending
segments.commentary: Management said about 90% plus of AUM is with Railways, at a NIM of about 1.3% (around 35 bps margin on cost-plus). Railway book is being replaced over time by higher-yield non-IR assets.

segments.name: Non-railway lending (diversification)
segments.commentary: Non-IR assets earn margins of 2-3.5 times the railway book, per management; INR35,000 crore of disbursement last year was non-IR. Pipeline covers metros, ports, renewables, thermal power, Gencos linked to Railways, and some road linkages, targeted for Q3 or early Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursements to exceed last year's level; guidance reiterated.
AUM target of near INR5 lakh crore (possibly slightly short by INR1,000-2,000 crore) by end FY27; management expects to show progress by Q3.
PAT expected to grow near 10% annually even with flat AUM, as non-IR assets replace railway assets at higher yields.

Railway-related funding of minimum about INR50,000 crore a year from FY28 for next decade, subject to the funding model (multilateral/aggregator role) to be finalised by end FY27; clearer numbers promised in Q3.
Mix target of 60% pure railways and 40% diversification by 2030.
Margin floor of INR0.85-0.90 per the ALM policy on non-railway loans; WACC target of 6.55% to be maintained.
capex_capacity: Management cited a Dedicated Freight Corridor from Dankuni to Surat (over 2,000 km, more than INR3 lakh crore), seven sanctioned high-speed rail corridors, and six freight lines planned under JV/PPP; total pie over INR20 lakh crore over about 10 years.
IRFC plans to act as sole financing arm and aggregator, with talks under way with the World Bank, other multilaterals and domestic players; model expected in place by end FY27.
Employee headcount roughly doubled in the last year, per the CEO.
demand_pricing: Floating-rate exposure: repo rate up 25 bps and back-to-back TONAR up 25 bps; management says it passes these through on non-railway loans and that resets are both ways.
Yen borrowing: about USD2 billion raised last year at around 1.8%, now about 2.25% after TONAR increases; hedging cost stated as not above 6.3%.
Term loans from banks are about 25% of the borrowing mix; management claims a 20-30 bps cushion against rate moves.
Prepayment: management said it sees no prepayment pressure, citing no prepayment penalty, no floor on benchmark-linked pricing, and lowest-in-market cost of funds.
Overhead cost cited at about INR0.15 per unit of lending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top execution priorities, and what are the main risks on railway capex, asset growth or funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 disbursements will exceed FY26, with non-IR pipeline (metros, ports, renewables, thermal, Gencos, roads) ready for Q3 or early Q4. Railway-linked funding is to start from FY28 at a minimum of INR50,000 crore a year, with the aggregator model to be set by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key financial risks (NIM, borrowing costs, asset quality) in a changing rate environment?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO cited a 6.55% WACC, lower than other NBFCs, and a push to raise more 54EC bonds and ECB. Management said the ALM team monitors margins weekly and keeps a minimum spread of INR0.85-0.90 on non-railway loans.

qa_highlights.question: How is non-railway lending priced, and how fast can rate increases be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Loans are priced on a cost-plus basis, and floating-rate loans reset monthly, quarterly or yearly. Management said a 25 bps repo hike and TONAR increase were passed through, and the company keeps a 20-30 bps cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Is there prepayment pressure, as seen at other government lenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no prepayment pressure, citing no prepayment penalty, no benchmark floor, and the cheapest funding in the market. Some prepayments by borrowers into IRFC were said to be business wins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM and disbursement vision, and is the INR5 lakh crore AUM target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated near INR5 lakh crore AUM by end FY27 (possibly 1,000-2,000 crore short), up from INR4.85 lakh crore at end FY26. It targets a 60:40 railway-to-diversified mix by 2030 and near-10% PAT growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the share price move so much, and what are the dividend and value prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said share price moves are outside its control and pointed to fundamentals. It cited an interim dividend of INR1.15 this year against INR1.05 last year, and a payout of about 40% of profit over the last two years.

risks_watch: Funding for the railway-linked pipeline (DFC, high-speed rail, freight lines) depends on a model yet to be finalised with the Ministry, multilaterals and bilaterals; no numbers given yet.
Rising floating rates (repo and TONAR each up 25 bps) and hardening yen hedge costs could squeeze spreads if pass-through lags.
AUM target near INR5 lakh crore may slip by INR1,000-2,000 crore; Q3 is the next checkpoint.
Non-IR loans are ticket-size lumpy (INR10,000-20,000 crore), so disbursement may be concentrated in H2.
Management did not disclose a specific Q2 standalone figure or asset-quality (GNPA/NPA) data in the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with a focus on growth, governance and shareholder returns. Management was firm on AUM and disbursement targets but vague on the railway funding model and gave few hard numbers beyond H1 growth rates. It answered the investor-relations question on share price with general market commentary.
key_quotes: So, the yield will be nearly 3 times of what we were doing with the Indian Railways.
numbers are not manufactured; they are earned.
We are not putting any prepayment penalty, whereas others.
PAT of this company will keep growing year-to-year on that line.
